task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2c) on REQ-171's implementation. REQ-171's own text explicitly names SECURITY-REVIEWER as a hard gate. This is the FIRST requirement where real host functions become reachable from guest code -- the actual attack surface REQ-166/167/168/169 were all built to defend, now exercised for real. Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req171-wasm-host-api-read.md) and the real shipped code (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex, the capability_gate.ex extension) in full before verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm every guest-memory access in host_api.ex genuinely goes through MemoryGuard.read/4 or write/4 -- grep for any direct Wasmex.Memory.* call in host_api.ex (should be zero hits outside MemoryGuard itself).

Confirm do_read_variable/6 reads from the closure-captured execution_context's variables map, never from a guest-supplied tenant/instance identifier -- the ONLY guest-supplied input should be the variable NAME (a string crossing via pointer/length), never which tenant/instance's variables to read.

Confirm do_log/8 attributes script/module identity, instance ID, and trace ID from the closure-captured execution_context, never from guest-supplied arguments -- a malicious guest must not be able to forge its own identity in a log entry.
Confirm no host function in host_api.ex calls Letflow.Repo at all, let alone with a guest-influenced prefix (grep for Repo.).

Confirm the capability_gate.ex extension's new :none sentinel genuinely cannot be used by a manifest to grant something it shouldn't -- read the widened import_descriptor()/capability_requirement() types and confirm :none-gated imports (now, uuid) are unconditionally present regardless of manifest content, matching the design's stated intent that these carry no confidentiality/integrity risk, not accidentally making them gate-bypassable for a DIFFERENT capability.

Confirm the guest-owns-the-buffer string-return protocol (design's sentinel scheme for read_variable's return path) cannot be abused by a guest supplying a malformed/adversarial buffer pointer or length to cause an out-of-bounds write on the HOST side -- trace the actual write path and confirm it goes through MemoryGuard.write/4's own bounds-checking, not a raw buffer copy.

Confirm the cross-runtime divergence CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already confirmed real (Lua denies capabilities at call-time, WASM denies at instantiation-time) has no security implication beyond what's already disclosed -- i.e., a module missing a granted capability still cannot instantiate and reach ANY host function, so the divergence is a timing/UX difference, not a security gap.

Cross-check against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8 explicitly -- INV-1 (tenant data isolation) and INV-3 (untrusted-runtime capability gating) are both squarely this diff's subject matter, more directly than any prior WASM requirement's SECURITY-REVIEWER pass, since this is the first requirement where a guest can actually read tenant data.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: REQ-171's shipped code (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex, lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex's REQ-171 extension) PASSES the security gate. Independently re-read both files in full (not the design doc's self-report), re-ran the greps the handoff specifies, and re-ran the real test suite (38/38 passed) and mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean) myself rather than trusting ELIXIR-DEV's or the design doc's claims.
verified_independently: Read lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex in full (366 lines) and lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex in full (434 lines) directly from the working tree on feature/WF02-REQ171-20260828 -- not from the design doc's description of what they should contain.

grep -n 'Wasmex.Memory' lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex -- 3 hits, all inert (a @typedoc reference to Wasmex.Memory.t(), a moduledoc prose sentence, and a code comment); zero actual Wasmex.Memory.* calls. Every real guest-memory touch in the file goes through MemoryGuard.read/4 (do_read_variable, read_log_field, read_log_context) or MemoryGuard.write/4 (write_buffer_result, the shared buffer-protocol helper used by do_read_variable/do_now/do_uuid).
grep -n 'Repo\.' on both host_api.ex and capability_gate.ex -- zero hits in either file. No host function touches Letflow.Repo, directly or via a guest-influenced prefix.

Read memory_guard.ex's read/4 and write/4 in full: both fetch the instance's live, current Wasmex.Memory.size/2 fresh (never cached), run check_bounds/3 (type/sign guard, offset-range check, end-of-range check using exact bignum arithmetic) before ever touching Wasmex.Memory.read_binary/write_binary, and return a structured {:error, {:invalid_pointer, _}} tuple on any failure -- never raises. write_buffer_result (host_api.ex lines 292-308) routes every write through MemoryGuard.write/4, including the out_cap-too-small probe path (writes an explicit <<>> so out_ptr is still bounds-checked at length 0) -- there is no raw buffer copy anywhere in the return-path implementation; a guest cannot cause an OOB host-side write by supplying an adversarial out_ptr/out_cap, since any invalid pointer is rejected by check_bounds/3 before any native memory call, and a too-small-but-valid out_cap is handled by writing zero bytes, not by writing n bytes into an undersized buffer.

Read do_read_variable/6 line by line: the only guest-supplied input consumed is (name_ptr, name_len), read via MemoryGuard.read/4 and UTF-8-validated; the lookup itself is Map.fetch(execution_context.variables, name) against the closure-captured execution_context -- no tenant_id, instance_id, or prefix is ever accepted as a separate guest-supplied argument, and execution_context.prefix is not even referenced by do_read_variable. A malicious guest can choose which variable NAME to read but has no mechanism to choose which tenant's/instance's variable map is consulted -- that is fixed at build_import_table/2 call time, structurally outside guest reach (INV-HOSTAPI-4, restated in the moduledoc and matching decision 0014(e) verbatim).

Read do_log/8 line by line: the metadata list's script_identity/instance_id/trace_id keys are populated exclusively from execution_context.script_identity/.instance_id/.trace_id (lines 237-239) -- guest-supplied bytes (level_ptr/level_len, message_ptr/message_len, context_ptr/context_len) feed only the level, message, and free-form context fields, never the three identity fields. A malicious guest cannot forge its own script/instance/trace identity in a log entry.

Read capability_gate.ex's @known_imports (lines 232-273), the widened import_descriptor()/capability_requirement() types (lines 139-182), and build_import_table/2's filter (line 304: Enum.filter(&(&1.capability == :none or MapSet.member?(granted, &1.capability)))). The :none tag is a fixed atom literal baked into the now/uuid rows of @known_imports at compile time -- a manifest's capabilities list is a [String.t()] (manifest.capabilities, matched via MapSet membership against string tokens only), so no manifest content can ever cause a DIFFERENT descriptor's string-typed capability requirement to be treated as :none or to bypass its own MapSet.member?/2 check. :none-gating is structurally isolated to the two rows the design names (now, uuid), both pure/side-effect-free per the design's stated rationale, and cannot be repurposed by manifest content to smuggle a grant for var:read/audit:log/service:call.

Traced the guest-owns-the-buffer protocol (design section 5.2) end to end against the real write_buffer_result implementation: no host function ever calls a guest alloc export (no re-entrant guest call exists anywhere in host_api.ex, confirmed by reading every do_* function), consistent with the design's stated reason for choosing this protocol (wasmex's own store-vs-caller deadlock warning for re-entrant calls).

Re-confirmed the cross-runtime divergence (Lua denies a missing capability at call-time; WASM denies at instantiation-time, per capability_gate.ex's own moduledoc and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step-01b pass) has no security implication beyond timing: build_import_table/1,2's filter means an import outside the granted set is structurally absent from the import table Wasmex.start_link/1 receives, and REQ-166/167's already-gate-approved instantiation mechanism means a module referencing an absent import fails to instantiate at all -- no guest code runs, so no host function (gated or :none) is reachable by a module lacking a required grant. The divergence is exactly the disclosed timing/UX difference (whole-module denial vs. per-call denial), not a path to reaching an ungranted host function.
mix compile --warnings-as-errors -- exit 0, clean, no output (re-run myself, not trusted from a prior report).

MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_test.exs test/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate_test.exs -- re-run myself with WASMEX_BUILD=true and the asdf/cargo PATH the design doc specifies: 38 tests, 38 passed, 0 failures, real output quoted above.
invariant_findings: INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, in the sense the handoff frames it: no new Ecto schema, table, or migration is touched by this diff (no schema-per-tenant :prefix mechanism is exercised), but this is the first requirement where a guest-reachable code path can read tenant-scoped runtime data (execution_context.variables). Verified PASS under (c)'s spirit -- the closure-captured execution_context is the only source of variables/instance_id/trace_id/script_identity data; no guest-supplied tenant/instance identifier is accepted anywhere in host_api.ex, so there is no attribution defect for a future caller to inherit. Actual per-tenant wiring of execution_context (mapping a real tenant/instance to the context closed over at build_import_table/2 call time) is explicitly out of this requirement's scope (design section 7, OQ-1) and deferred to a future dispatch-integration requirement -- that future requirement will need its own INV-1 check once it exists, since it is the one that will actually populate execution_context from real tenant state.
INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type or client-facing serialization is touched; S4 has not started.

INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) -- APPLIES, squarely, and PASS. This is the first requirement wiring real host functions into the WASM capability-gated import table. Verified: every host function's presence in the import table Wasmex.start_link/1 receives is gated by REQ-167's already-approved manifest-derived whitelist (build_import_table/1,2); no function in host_api.ex performs ambient network/filesystem access (read_variable/log/now/uuid touch only guest memory via MemoryGuard, Logger, Ecto.Lua.Platform.now/0's clock, and Ecto.UUID.generate/0 -- no Repo, no HTTP, no File); the :none sentinel is structurally confined to the two rows it is defined for (see verified_independently above) and cannot be abused to grant a different capability.

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES (live invariant). grep for System.get_env/password/secret/token in both changed files: only doc-prose hits describing capability tokens as 'opaque string tokens' -- no hardcoded secret material, no System.get_env usage needed by this diff. PASS.
INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) -- NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4 has not started.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- satisfied by this handoff itself: this result explicitly states which of INV-1..INV-8 apply and how each is satisfied, per INV-6's own how-to-verify.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE to this diff's own content (no Repo.query/Ecto raw SQL anywhere in host_api.ex or capability_gate.ex; grep confirmed zero hits), but trivially PASS since the invariant's condition (any Repo.query hit) is absent.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES (live invariant) and PASS. grep for the bare '{:ok, ...} = ' pattern in both files: zero hits. Independently confirmed every do_* function is total by construction: do_read_variable/do_now/do_uuid route all MemoryGuard failures through explicit {:error, _} matches (or the with/else clause) that return -2 rather than raise; do_log has no failure-signaling channel at all (results: []) and its own design explicitly substitutes fixed placeholder strings / nil / context_decode_error: true metadata on any MemoryGuard or JSON-decode failure rather than raising -- Jason.decode/1 (not decode!/1) is used specifically to keep that call site non-raising. This matches INV-HOSTAPI-2's binding requirement, itself necessary because Finding 3 (design section 1) establishes that a raising callback and a type-mismatched return are indistinguishable from an ordinary WASM trap at the wasmex layer -- correctness has to come from the callback body, and it does.
result.gaps_found: None blocking. One forward-looking note, not a defect in this diff: INV-1's full closure (real tenant data reaching execution_context.variables, keyed correctly per tenant/instance) is not yet exercised because no caller wires build_import_table/2 with a real execution_context yet (design OQ-1, explicitly deferred) -- the next requirement that adds that wiring is the one SECURITY-REVIEWER must scrutinize hardest for INV-1, since that is where a real cross-tenant leak could first be introduced (e.g. resolving the wrong instance's variables map). This diff itself introduces no such path and correctly keeps execution_context fully guest-opaque.
